name: inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-pulp-timer-zipdma-4w-branch-f1f6
notes: trigger_writes and status_offsets repeat the values already used by configs/scenarios/inprocess-irq-pulp-timer-profile.json; the entry re-checks them against the timer register map and interrupt declarations
dma_window must not overlap the APB target window; the timer owns 0x40000000..0x40000fff
the timer declares 50 MHz, the CPU 50 MHz and the ZipDMA a nominal 1 Hz simulation rate, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives all three models

f1_program_words 4 declares a four-word F1 program in the fixed trampoline slot and f1_allow_branches admits strictly-forward B-type branches (opcode 0x63, funct3 0/1/4/5/6/7).  The target is kSlot + 4*i + sext(bimm), must be 4-byte aligned and strictly forward, and must stay inside the installed image; target == kSlot + 4*words (the appended return jump) is the legal exit.  A branch program legally skips words, so the case's evidence is the in-slot RVFI retirement trace: prog_retires and prog_trace_count, the strictly increasing prog_pc_order, and prog_trace_hash (FNV-1a 32 over pc/insn/rd/wdata) compared with the Python reference trace built from f1_reference_expectation.  JAL/JALR, CSR, compressed parcels, loops and out-of-image branches are refused by name.  Evidence: runs/round1-f1-b/ (fixed-branch, fuzz-20).
